split_off.caption: Back stitching by one rule on the stitch records of each design (tools/underlay_cover): thread is drawn in sew order at 0.4 mm; a stitch most of whose thread ends up under thread sewn at least six stitches later is back stitching, and its pattern is read from its own shape (a run, a zigzag -- sawtooth or this engine's ladder -- or lattice rows). 'Sitting on thread' is the share of the top thread's area that already had thread under it. MARINE is the bottom 32% of each design's height; 'inside the stroke' is a hole more than 1 mm from the sewn area's edge, so on a satin stem it is a split point or back stitching, never a rail. Column legs by tools/satin_columns' cross detector. Ours is 100 mm wide, the pro's hat file 101.9.
